display_name: The Martyrs of the Pantokrator Monastery at Daou Pendeli

death.note: The only year on the page, in the brackets its day line closes with: «Прмчч. многих священной обители Пантократора, в Дау Пендели (Аттика) пострадавших (ок. 1680).»

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 10 апреля ст. ст. — «Прмчч. многих священной обители Пантократора, в Дау Пендели (Аттика) пострадавших (ок. 1680).»
source.note: The line carries no typikon icon, so no rank is recorded. It enumerates nobody — «многих», many, is the whole of its reckoning — so it is one entry and not a folder for each, by the ruling in docs/CORPUS.md §10.1 on a company a source does not name. The entry behind the line, name page 14999, is an index page carrying the heading and the day and no life.

attestations.note: **No «ru» name form is stored, on purpose.** What the calendar prints is a description and not a name: the index entry heads them «Прмчч. обители Пантократора, в Дау Пендели», and with the rank abbreviation taken off what is left is a genitive phrase that is not a nominative form of anything. Expanding «Прмчч.» and keeping it, as martyrs-of-martyropolis keeps «Μάρτυρες εν Μαρτυροπόλει», would both reconstruct an abbreviation and add a fifth row to the gate’s hand-held list of companies whose rank is their name, which is a code change. A language with no recorded form is left out rather than filled, per docs/CORPUS.md §3.
Not checked: doxologia.ro for the corresponding civil day (7 October 2026).

saint.gr’s page for 10 Απριλίου, the same menologion day, was read and does not name them; no other Greek day was searched for them, and the Greek church keeps them, so this is a gap and not a refusal (7 October 2026).
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (7 October 2026).
